text: Eutychus, whose name means "good fortune," fell asleep while Paul preached and fell from the third story. Grace is the highest floor.
explanation:
A young man named Eutychus (literally good fortune) sat in a window of a third-floor room while Paul preached late into the night. He sank into a deep sleep, fell, and was taken up dead. It's a picture of how the church loses its good fortune: by falling asleep to Paul's revelation, the gift of righteousness and complete forgiveness by grace.

People think of grace as kindergarten, a ground floor to graduate from. But Paul says those who turn back to the law to be justified "have fallen from grace." You can only fall from something higher. Grace is the top floor. Paul went down, embraced the young man, and brought him back to life. Let that revelation embrace you, and stay on the highest floor.

text: God made Adam last, so his first full day was a day of rest. You begin by enjoying a finished work.
explanation:
God created everything first: the light, the land, the gardens and the fruit trees. Only then did He form man, and then He rested, not because He was tired, but because the work was complete. Adam had no part in creating any of it, so he could take no credit. His part was simply to enjoy.

That's still God's way. Jesus sent His disciples to "a large upper room, furnished and prepared." Through the cross, everything you need has already been prepared. Your part is to step in and enjoy His finished work.

text: A vine has no trunk; it's all branches. "I am the vine, you are the branches" means His life is your life.
explanation:
A tree has a trunk with separate branches growing out of it. A grapevine is different: it's simply branches twisted together. When Jesus says, "I am the vine, you are the branches," He's saying we're wrapped up in Him so completely that the same life, power and peace that flows through Him flows through you.

How can the vine be rich and the branch poor? How can the vine be healthy and the branch sick, or the vine at peace while the branch frets? The only thing that restricts the sap is tightening up: stress, grasping, trying to handle it yourself. When you let go, God takes hold.

text: When God gave the law at Sinai, 3,000 died. When He gave the Spirit at Pentecost, 3,000 were saved.
explanation:
The law was given at Mount Sinai around the feast later known as Pentecost, and that day 3,000 people died. Centuries later, on the day of Pentecost, the Holy Spirit fell in an upper room on Mount Zion, and 3,000 people were saved.

"The letter kills, but the Spirit gives life." Much of the church has camped at Sinai, memorising what we must and mustn't do. But in the upper room on Zion, Jesus gave church truths of pure supply: the Comforter, His peace, "I call you friends," "love one another as I have loved you." Spend your time on Zion.

text: "He leads me in the paths of righteousness": in Hebrew, circular tracks. The Shepherd lifts you higher while you graze.
explanation:
The word for paths, ma'gal, speaks of a circular track. A wise shepherd doesn't drive his flock straight up a steep slope, where they'd tire and scatter. He leads them around the hill in gentle circles, and they eat as they go. They hardly notice they're climbing, until they find themselves at the top, where the air is fresh.

As you feed on the truth of righteousness, you rise above your troubles without strain. Even Jesus "went about doing good" in a circuit around Galilee. You may feel you're going in circles right now. Keep grazing on His word, and one day you'll look around and realise how high He's brought you.

text: "Keep them through Your name": Father. There's love, and protection, in that name.
explanation:
God has many glorious names: El Shaddai, El Elyon, Jehovah Rapha, Jehovah Shalom. All of them are summed up in the one Jesus came to reveal. "I have declared to them Your name… that the love with which You loved Me may be in them." And, "Holy Father, keep through Your name those whom You have given Me."

The more you call Him Father, the more you sense that He loves you as He loves Jesus. And there's protection under that name. Some days you won't even know what to pray. Just say, "Abba, Father." He hears that, and He answers.

text: "As the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you." He never grows bored of you.
explanation:
Notice what God doesn't say: "as a husband rejoices over his wife of many years." Over time, marriages can drift into routine, and romance fades. Instead He says, as a bridegroom over his bride, with the fresh, overflowing delight of the wedding day itself.

That's how He feels about you today, and every day. Not tolerated, not merely put up with, but rejoiced over. His passion for you never grows stale. "He will rejoice over you with gladness, He will quiet you with His love, He will rejoice over you with singing."
